name: Model Theory
description: A lens for composing Factors from the language of formal languages, structures, and the relationship between syntax and semantics. Maps model-theoretic concepts—signatures, theories, models, definability, types, stability, and forking—to the 19-node topology. Useful for Factors involving formal systems, interpretations, classification of structures, and the interplay between axioms and their models.

x.note: The depth anchor—every finitely satisfiable theory is satisfiable. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking compactness to type space, types, and Löwenheim‑Skolem.

y.note: The relational anchor—if a theory has an infinite model, it has models of all infinite cardinalities. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, tying Löwenheim‑Skolem to compactness, type space, and types.

z.note: The transformational anchor—truth cannot be defined within the same language. Persistently connected to 0 (theory), reflecting that the theory (object language) is separate from the metalanguage where truth is defined.

0.note: The set of sentences closed under consequence. Persistently connected to z (Tarski's undefinability), linking the theory to the impossibility of defining its own truth.

1.note: The boundary—vocabulary of the language. Part of the 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1, connecting signature to elementary embeddings, definable sets, and elements.

2.note: Primitives—individuals in a structure's domain. Completes the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, showing how elements are embedded in signature, elementary embeddings, and definable sets.

3.note: The invariant law—axioms defining the class of models. A node in the 7‑core; connected to stability (c) and quantifier elimination (e), as axioms determine stability and whether quantifier elimination holds.

4.note: The fundamental relation—satisfaction between structures and formulas. A node in the 7‑core; connected to forking (b) and monster model (f), as forking is defined via satisfaction, and the monster model is the universal domain of satisfaction.

5.note: The pattern—sets definable by formulas. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, bridging elementary embeddings and elements.

6.note: The transformation—embedding preserving all first‑order formulas. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, connecting signature to definable sets.

7.note: The realization—a structure satisfying the theory. Persistently connected to 8 (cardinality), linking the model to its size.

8.note: The granularity—size of the model. Persistently connected to 7 (model), reflecting that the model's cardinality is a key invariant.

9.note: The event—complete set of formulas consistent with the theory. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, placing types between compactness, type space, and Löwenheim‑Skolem.

a.note: Pure potential—Stone space of complete n‑types. Initiates the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking type space to compactness, types, and Löwenheim‑Skolem.

b.note: The arena—non‑forking independence relation. A node in the 7‑core; connected to satisfaction (4) and prime/saturated model (d), as forking defines independence and is used to construct prime models.

c.note: Directional bias—property that the theory has few types. A node in the 7‑core; connected to axioms (3) and monster model (f), as stability is a property of the theory and is witnessed in the monster.

d.note: Persistent structure—models with special properties. A node in the 7‑core; connected to forking (b) and monster model (f), as prime models are built using forking, and the monster is saturated.

e.note: The active algorithm—procedure eliminating quantifiers. A node in the 7‑core; connected to axioms (3) and monster model (f), as quantifier elimination is a property of the theory and is often proved in the monster.

f.note: The resonant cavity—large saturated model containing all others. A node in the 7‑core; connected to satisfaction (4), stability (c), prime/saturated (d), quantifier elimination (e), and the rest, forming the central hub of model‑theoretic universality.

n.interpretation: Model complexity / Morley rank / Shelah classification

values.n=1: Stable — no order property, types have ranks
values.n=5: o‑minimal — ordered structures, definable sets are finite unions of intervals

n.formula: n corresponds to the 'tameness' level in classification theory

m.interpretation: Type space dimension / Number of non‑isomorphic models

values.m=0: Categorical in some cardinality — unique model up to isomorphism
values.m=1: Few models — finite number in each cardinality

m.formula: m = log₂(κ) where κ is number of models in some cardinality

phase.formula: φ = 2π × (realized types / total types in Stone space)
phase.special: Phase = 0 when all types are realized (saturated model); phase = π when only isolated types are realized (prime model)
phase.significance: Phase measures the 'richness' of the model in terms of which types are realized.

syntactic.description: The Factor viewed as a formal theory (sentences, axioms, consequences)
syntactic.phase_condition: Phase as consistency—0 for consistent theory, π for inconsistent

semantic.description: The Factor viewed as a structure (domain, interpretations)
semantic.phase_condition: Phase as elementarity—0 for elementary substructure, π for elementary extension

geometric.description: The Factor viewed as a geometry of definable sets (Zariski‑like)
geometric.phase_condition: Phase as dimension—0 for minimal, π for maximal

creating_anew.note: When creating a logical theory, start with signature (node 1), axioms (node 3), and models (node 7). Let types (node 9) classify elements.

translating_known.group_theory: Map groups: signature {·, e, ⁻¹}, axioms of group theory as node 3, models as groups
translating_known.arithmetic_PA: Map Peano Arithmetic: signature {0, S, +, ×}, induction schema as node 5, standard model ℕ as node 7
translating_known.real_closed_fields: Map RCF: signature {+, ×, 0, 1, <}, o‑minimal as node c, ℝ as node 7
translating_known.ZFC_set_theory: Map ZFC: signature {∈}, cumulative hierarchy V as node d, forcing extensions as node b

temporary_note.special: A signature defined, but axioms not yet specified. Awaiting the laws that will define the class of structures.

constraints.compactness: Node x ensures every finitely consistent theory is consistent.
constraints.löwenheim_skolem: Node y ensures infinite models exist in all cardinalities.
constraints.truth_definition: Node z ensures object language truth is not definable in itself.
constraints.stratum_preference: global for foundational model theory; trefoil_c for stable theories; trefoil_g for o‑minimal; fig8 for unstable, NIP
constraints.invariant_core: The Model Theory paradigm respects the persistent skeleton from trefoil_i, which decomposes into five subsystems: (1) edge 0→z linking theory to Tarski's undefinability, (2) edge 8→7 linking cardinality to model, (3) 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x linking compactness–type space–type–Löwenheim‑Skolem, (4) 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1 linking signature–elementary embedding–definable set–element, and (5) 7‑node core {3,4,b,c,d,e,f} encoding the heart of model theory: axioms–satisfaction–forking–stability–prime/saturated model–quantifier elimination–monster model.
